title: Entities in a linked list
description:
Keep game entities in a doubly linked list so removing one in the middle is cheap.

```
spawn goblin, orc, bat
remove orc (while walking the list) -> goblin, bat
walk backwards: bat, goblin
```
hints: Unlinking: `if (e->prev) e->prev->next = e->next; else m_head = e->next;` and the mirror for `next` and `m_tail` (lesson 3.06).
`for (Entity* e{m_head}; e;) { Entity* next{e->next}; ... e = next; }` survives deleting `e`.
requirements: `struct Entity { std::string name; Entity* prev; Entity* next; };` owned by a `List` class.
`spawn` adds at the end; `remove` unlinks and deletes.
Removing during a walk is safe because you keep `next` before deleting.
stretch: Compare the speed with `std::vector` and erasing for 10,000 entities.
